title: Differential rate-slicing: hierarchical entitlements + billing acceptance criteria
creator: Maya Torres
description: Introduce a differential rate-slicing model that allows hierarchical entitlements across organization -> team -> route, ties per-route compute multipliers (model/quantization) to billing, and supports soft-overage grace windows. Deliver API, Console UX, billing pipelines, and migration tooling. This ticket captures PRD-level requirements and acceptance criteria for engineering and finance to implement and validate the change.
problem_statement: Current plan entitlements are flat (per-customer token/embedding buckets or credits) and cannot express per-route or per-team priorities. Customers want predictable budgets for critical routes while allowing cheaper best-effort workloads to burst. Finance needs accurate per-call compute attribution for invoicing (different models and quantization have different cost profiles). Existing billing metrics do not support hierarchical translations or soft-overage grace credits, causing manual reconciliation and opaque invoices.
goals: Define and implement hierarchical entitlements: organization -> team -> route with inheritance and override rules.
Enable per-route compute multipliers so bills reflect model/precision choices (e.g., llama-70b-8q -> x1.0, llama-13b-fp16 -> x0.35).
Support 'rate-slicing' policies that let operators allocate a fraction of a team's entitlement to high-priority routes with guaranteed concurrency and separate soft overage buckets.
Produce billing-accurate token/compute attribution and a reconciliation pipeline that reconciles usage to invoices with automated test fixtures.
Deliver Console UI for admins to view, edit and preview entitlement inheritance and to simulate invoice impacts.
Provide a migration tool to map existing plans into the new hierarchy with conservative defaults and rollback path.
non_goals: Designing new pricing tiers or public price changes as part of this ticket (handled by Pricing Strategy team).
Full policy language for organization-wide complex multi-tenant billing (that will be follow-up).
Implementing support for reserved capacity contract accounting — that remains in Dedicated billing scope.
Deep ML model cost estimation research beyond implementing configurable multipliers and a small sample-validated multiplier table.
requirements: API: Add entitlement APIs: create/get/update organization/team/route entitlements; returns inherited effective_entitlement with source tags (inherited/overridden).
API: Per-call usage payload must include route_id, model_id, quantization_tag, and caller_team_id for correct attribution.
Billing pipeline: Apply compute_multiplier by model_id+quantization to raw tokens to produce billable_compute_units. Multipliers are configurable via admin API and versioned.

Soft-overage: Implement per-team soft_overage_bucket that can be consumed with configurable grace window (hours) and automatic rollback to main bucket once window expires. Soft-overage usage is flagged for reporting and eligible for automatic refunds if used during service incidents.
Console: Entitlement editor that shows effective limits at each level, visual inheritance chain, and an invoice preview button that simulates last-30d usage costs under proposed changes.
Observability: Expose metrics and dashboards: billable_compute_units_by_team, overage_events, entitlement_hits_missed, invoice_simulation_delta.

Migration: CLI tool and one-off job to convert existing per-customer credits into org/team/route entitlements following rule set (default: 90% to org, 9% to team, 1% reserve for high-priority routes).
Security: RBAC checks so only org admins can change org-level entitlements; team leads can change team/route-level entitlements if permitted by org policy.

Finance integration: Billing pipeline outputs line items compatible with invoicing service: {customer_id, period, line_item_type, units, multiplier, raw_tokens, billable_compute_units, rate}, and example invoice templates updated.

Test coverage: Unit tests for multiplier application, integration tests for end-to-end attribution (call -> billing line item), and a set of reconciliation fixtures comparing simulated invoice to expected values.
Backward compatibility: If request lacks team_id, fallback to previous flat-billing behavior and emit a warning-event to stream for migration telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: API returns effective_entitlement and shows inheritance source for 95% of sample orgs in migration test data.
AC2: Billing pipeline multiplies tokens by configured multiplier for at least 5 validated model+quantization pairs and produces expected billable_compute_units within 1% of test oracle.
AC3: Console entitlement editor allows edit/preview and the invoice preview delta matches billing pipeline simulation for three test customers (small/medium/enterprise) within 2%.

AC4: Soft-overage behavior: create a scenario where a team consumes its main bucket, falls into soft_overage bucket during a 6-hour grace window, and billing flags the soft_overage usage separately; finance-run refund scenario triggers when an incident tag is attached to that window.
AC5: Migration tool produces a mapping report for 100 migrated customers with no missing entitlements and a rollback script that restores original credit records if requested.

AC6: Monitoring: dashboards show billable_compute_units_by_team in production-sim environment; alerting rules created for >5% daily delta between simulated and actual billed units during canary period.
AC7: Security: attempted changes to org-level entitlements by non-admins are rejected; audit logs show actor, timestamp, and diff for every entitlement write during test runs.
AC8: Finance integration: sample generated invoices for three customers include line items with multiplier metadata and match accounting ledger schema; billing team signs off on sample invoices.

AC9: Backward compatibility: requests without team_id continue to be billed under flat model and produce a migration-warning event; no more than 0.1% of production traffic should experience a different billed amount compared to baseline during canary.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): Implement API, multiplier table, and unit tests. Internal CI runs with synthetic data.
Phase 1 (canary): Enable for 1% of customers with opt-in flag; run billing pipeline in shadow mode for 14 days and compare simulated invoices.
Phase 2 (beta): Offer as opt-in feature for self-serve customers; provide migration CLI and console preview. Finance team performs manual invoice reconciliations for first 50 customers.
Phase 3 (ga): Flip default for new customers; offer migration window for existing customers. Monitor reconciliation alerts for 30 days and keep rollback path available.
metrics: Billable compute accuracy: median(abs(simulated_bill - actual_bill)/actual_bill) during canary <= 3%
Migration success rate: >= 99% of customers migrated with no missing entitlements
Overage disputes: reduce finance disputes related to per-route attribution by 80% in first quarter
Adoption: percent of eligible customers enabling hierarchical entitlements within 60 days of GA
Latency: entitlement API p95 <= 50ms for read operations
dependencies: PM-79212: pricing-strategy-multipliers (approved multiplier suggestions from Finance)
SEC-4201: entitlement-audit-logging (audit log storage and retention)
FIN-001: sample invoice templates and GL mapping approval
notes: Trade-offs discussed: We intentionally avoid introducing per-model dynamic pricing rules (e.g., time-of-day surge pricing) in v1 to limit billing complexity.
Open question: How to represent fractional multipliers on invoices (show raw_tokens, multiplier, billable_units) — prefer transparent three-column line items.
Edge case: multi-tenant customers using shared auth tokens need mapping to team_id; interim plan is to require explicit caller_team_id in SDKs and emit warnings in server logs.
Finance feedback: prefer deterministic multipliers and versioned change logs to avoid retroactive billing surprises.
Design feedback: Console preview should include example invoice PDF export and a delta heatmap per route.
